04 / HARDWARE CONCEPT

VST Pedal

Off the desk.
On the floor.

What if your favourite Windows VST plug-ins could come to the gig? An idea for a standalone guitar pedal that brings a DAW’s sounds into a live rig.

Inside the idea ↗Concept only · No prototype or download yet
CONCEPT VISUALISATION / NOT A FINISHED PRODUCT

THE QUESTION

Why should your
sound stay at home?

DAWs put a world of guitar effects within reach. Taking those exact sounds to a live show often means bringing a computer along, too.

The idea is a guitar pedal that runs Windows VST plug-ins itself: a physical home for a software signal chain, built around the way you play.

This is an early concept. Hardware, plug-in compatibility, latency, controls and release plans are still to be worked out. The model shows a possible direction, not a working prototype.

01 / THE SOUND

Your existing plug-ins.

Explore whether familiar Windows VST effects can live in a dedicated pedal format.

02 / THE FEEL

Made for the floor.

Find the right balance of tactile controls, a footswitch, and a readable live interface.

03 / THE CHALLENGE

Ready for a real stage.

Investigate audio latency, reliability and plug-in hosting before promising a product.
